comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose the specific impact of inventory write-downs and releases on gross margin. NVDA provides quantitative specifics, stating that provisions totaled $2.2 billion and resulted in unfavorable gross margin impacts of 2.7% in 2024 and 7.5% in 2023. AMD discloses the qualitative mechanism and risk, noting that additional inventory write-downs would negatively impact gross margin, while selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value results in a net benefit to gross margin. Both firms address the same financial driver (inventory valuation adjustments) and its direct effect on gross margin metrics.

sentences.text: Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $2.2 billion for both fiscal years 2024 and 2023.
The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.
